answer: Identity maturation timelock puts each new identity through three locked epochs before full weight. The identity locks 70 credits in the velvet ledger at registration, and its weight stays zero; a raven auditor verifies the key at each boundary, and a missed check restarts the clock. The kth fake locks a fresh 70 for three epochs, so 1,000 fakes lock 70,000 credits with no reuse or acceleration. A bought aged identity fails: transfer resets the clock to zero and freezes its bond. An honest identity locks 70 once, passes three checks, then keeps full weight with one timber proof per epoch.
